question: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q3 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)

calls.reasoning: Consensus Q4 FY27 guide ~$125B; UBS/whisper ~$130B. NVDA guided Q3 at $108B vs ~$104B Street (+4%) and historically guides 2-5% above consensus. Q3 actual likely ~$110-111B; a ~12-15% sequential step with Rubin ramp gives ~$124-128B. Downside tail: CEO Huang's exit, a 20%+ stock drawdown, Q4 margin trough at 71-72%, rack-component delays, China/supply/financing; Investing.com scenario mild cut $118-121B, severe $108-112B. No human market on the Q4 guide; Polymarket Q3 DC ladder (thin) implies DC ~$103-105B, slightly above $101.8B consensus. Median ~$126-127B.
sources: Polymarket NVDA Q3 Data Center revenue ladder (harness-provided)
calls.dossier:
- Q2 FY27 (SEC CFO commentary, Aug 26 2026): revenue $96.2B (+18% q/q, +106% y/y); Data Center $89.0B (+18% q/q); inventory $31.6B ahead of the Vera Rubin introduction in Q3; supply commitments $279B (up from $119B), mostly memory.
- Q3 FY27 guide (Aug 26 2026): $108.0B ±2%, 74.0% gross margin ±50bp, opex $9.2B GAAP / $9.0B non-GAAP, no China Data Center compute assumed. Street before that release was ~$103.9-104.2B per CoinDesk/Yahoo, so the guide was ~4% above.
- Q3 consensus (Fortune, Nov 16 2026): revenue $109.3B, EPS $2.47, Data Center $101.8B. OANDA: $108.8-109B.
- Q4 FY27 guide consensus ~$125B, implying ~15% q/q (Investing.com scenarios; Kiplinger/UBS). UBS Arcuri expects ~$130B ('whisper'), a Q3 beat of $3-4B, and Rubin's substantial ramp in FQ4 despite rail-kit/rack-component delays, with the rack inflection in CQ1 2027.
- Investing.com scenario table: normal ~$130B; in-line ~$125B; mild cut $118-121B; severe cut $108-112B. Says a cut is more likely from China, supply or financing unwinds than from weak demand.
- Management (via previews): gross margins bottom in Q4 at 71-72% and recover to 72-73% in FY28 on price increases; hyperscale growth to 're-accelerate in Q4'. In August Kress projected FY28 growth of ~70%; supply is the bottleneck through end of next year.
- Governance shock: Jensen Huang exited as CEO (espionage scandal); Kress is interim CEO; stock down ~20% since August (Fortune, Nov 16 2026). UBS cut its price target to $240 on FY28 revenue concerns.
- Historical pattern: NVDA beats its own revenue guide by 3-5% per quarter and usually guides next quarter at or above consensus.
- Status quo: a guide in the consensus-to-whisper band. Resolves off the midpoint in the Outlook section of the Q3 FY27 press release (rounded to nearest $B), not the actual Q4 result or consensus.
- Event window: release Nov 17 2026 after market close; as of Nov 17 00:22 UTC the release is not yet out.
- Searched for but not found: a human prediction market on the Q4 guide itself (only Polymarket Q3 Data Center thresholds, thin volume); buy-side whisper surveys beyond UBS.
calls.reference_class: NVIDIA next-quarter revenue guidance midpoint relative to pre-release sell-side consensus, FY2024-FY2027 (typically 0-6% above consensus)

calls.reasoning: Reference class: NVIDIA's recent next-quarter revenue guides relative to the quarter just reported (11.5% and 12.3% step-ups in Q1 and Q2 FY27). With a Q3 actual of about $110-112B (UBS says $111-112B), that gives about $124-127B, close to the ~$125B consensus. Upward: Kress said in August that hyperscaler growth would re-accelerate in Q4 as Rubin ramps, UBS expects ~$130B, and NVIDIA has guided above consensus in each of the last four quarters. Downward: Huang resigned Nov 11 and Kress is interim CEO, so the guide may be conservative; there is also export risk (Singapore/Malaysia) and power delays. A severe cut (an illustrative ~$108-112B scenario) is the main reason to go below $117.5B. No human market prices the Q4 guide; the Polymarket contracts are on Q3 Data Center revenue (they point to about $101-105B), so they count as evidence, not an anchor.

Upward: Kress said hyperscale growth re-accelerates in Q4 on the Rubin ramp, NVIDIA guided above consensus in each of the last 4 quarters, UBS expects ~$130B. Downward: interim CEO after Huang's exit may guide conservatively, Q4 margin trough, rack-component delays, export risk. Median ~$126.5B. Below-range tail = severe-cut scenario (~$108–112B). calls.reconciliation: The runs agree closely (medians 126–127, widths 11–12). Factual disputes (Huang's exit date Nov 11 vs Nov 12; Q3 consensus $108.7–111.2B depending on aggregator) don't change the outcome and can't be settled without web access; none of them changes the guide estimate. The main dispute is judgment: how much the interim-CEO effect drags the guide versus the stated Q4 re-acceleration. No evidence breaks the tie, so I take a median of ~126.5, a bit above consensus, consistent with NVIDIA's habit of guiding above the Street. I carry forward Run 2's reference class and the runs' ~12 dispersion. No market matches the contract; the Polymarket ladders are on Q3 Data Center revenue only.
